Constants linking the lengthscale to the approximate GP settings

Source: R/create.R
gp_approx_constants.Rd

Constants from Riutort-Mayol et al. (2023, Section 4.3.1) doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2 . With half-range S, boundary factor c and m basis functions, lengthscales l are approximated accurately when m >= m_factor * c * S / l and c >= c_factor * l / S (with c >= 1.2). The paper does not cover Matern 1/2 (equivalently, the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck kernel). Its m_factor is derived by repeating the paper's simulation procedure (see the hsgp_m_c_relationship folder, branch matern-half-m-c-relationship, of https://github.com/sbfnk-bot/basis_functions_approach_to_GP). The same procedure reproduced the squared exponential and Matern 3/2 and 5/2 constants to within 8-13%. Matern 1/2 is the roughest kernel, so it needs the most basis functions. Its c_factor was not independently validated and uses the Matern 3/2 value. The periodic kernel has no boundary and needs m >= m_factor * S / l basis functions (Appendix B), so its c_factor is NA.

Usage

gp_approx_constants(gp_type, nu)

Arguments

gp_type

Integer kernel type as used in the Stan model (0: squared exponential, 1: periodic, 2: Matern).

nu

Numeric Matern order.

Value

A list with elements m_factor and c_factor.
